title: The Crab and Its Mother
text:
A mother crab was watching her young one scuttle across the wet sand. It moved the way all crabs move, sideways, dragging its legs at an angle and twisting its body as it went.

"Why do you walk so crookedly, child?" she said. "It is far more becoming to walk straight ahead. Hold yourself properly and go forward like a respectable creature."

The young crab stopped and looked at her. "I would be glad to, Mother," it said. "Just show me how. Walk straight in front of me, and I promise I will follow your steps exactly."

The mother crab set out to demonstrate. She lifted one leg and then another, pushed forward, and found herself sliding off sideways just as her child had done. She tried again and again, and every time the result was the same.

In the end she gave up, and said nothing more to her child about the way it walked.
lesson: Children copy what we do far more than what we say. Before correcting a habit in them, check whether they learned it from you.
